truePeak.label: True peak
truePeak.why: 4x-oversampled peak (BS.1770); the master limiter ceiling is -1 dBTP, above 0 dBTP a lossy encode or DAC clips.

clipRuns.label: Clipped runs
clipRuns.why: Runs of 2+ consecutive samples at or above 0.999 full scale.

dcOffset.label: DC offset
dcOffset.why: Mean sample value, floored at -80 dBFS (below that it is rounding noise, not DC); DC wastes headroom and thumps on start/stop.

loudnessTarget.label: Integrated loudness vs target
loudnessTarget.why: Whole-song BS.1770 integrated loudness against the style target in js/loudness.js (-10 club / -14 quiet / -16 classical).

lra.label: Loudness range
lra.why: EBU Tech 3342 LRA of the whole song; very large values mean sections a listener has to ride the volume for. Club/pop styles only.

lraClassical.label: Loudness range (classical)
lraClassical.why: The same LRA for the classical styles, where 15-25 LU is normal for concert recordings (EBU R128 s1); only beyond that is the piece unlistenable without riding the volume.

limiterStrain.label: Limiter strain
limiterStrain.why: Share of 10 ms frames where the master limiter takes more than 3 dB (squashed transients, pumping).

limiterDeep.label: Deepest gain reduction (1st pct)
limiterDeep.why: Gain reduction exceeded in 1% of frames.

limiterJump.label: Gain-reduction jump (p99)
limiterJump.why: Frame-to-frame change in limiter gain; fast big swings are audible as distortion or pumping.

tiltBright.label: Spectral tilt (too bright)
tiltBright.why: Slope of octave-band energy 63 Hz-16 kHz (pink noise = 0). Mixed music sits well below 0; near or above 0 reads as thin and bright.

tiltDark.label: Spectral tilt (too dark)
tiltDark.why: Same slope from the other side: steeper than -10 dB/oct is a muffled, blanket-over-the-speaker mix.

mud.label: Low-mid build-up (200-500 Hz)
mud.why: Per-octave energy of 200-500 Hz over the louder of its neighbours (60-200 Hz, 500 Hz-2 kHz). Low mids standing well above both the bass and the mids sound boxy and muddy.

harsh.label: Presence vs mids (2-5 kHz)
harsh.why: Per-octave energy of 2-5 kHz over 500 Hz-2 kHz. The ear is most sensitive at 2-5 kHz; when it carries more energy per octave than the mids the mix is harsh and fatiguing.

subShare.label: Sub share (20-60 Hz)
subShare.why: Share of energy below 60 Hz; style-dependent, so only gated as drift from baseline.

monoLoss.label: Mono fold-down loss
monoLoss.why: Loudness change when L and R are summed to mono (phone speakers, club mono-sum); big losses mean phase cancellation.

correlation.label: L/R correlation (5th pct of 400 ms blocks)
correlation.why: Phase correlation of loud blocks. Wide reverb and pads sit near 0 (fine: -3 dB in mono); strongly negative blocks lose 6+ dB or vanish when summed to mono.

lowSide.label: Side energy under 120 Hz
lowSide.why: Bass width relative to bass mono; club rigs and vinyl want mono lows. Not applied to orchestral seating.

kickBass.label: Bass under the kick (p90)
kickBass.why: Bass-stem energy under 120 Hz in the 60 ms after each kick, relative to the kick: high means the two fight instead of ducking or interlocking.

missingParts.label: Silent parts that have notes
missingParts.why: A part the sequencer played at least twice in the window whose stem stayed below -70 dBFS.

masking.label: Most-masked part
masking.why: Share of a part's energy in time/third-octave cells where the rest of the mix is 10 dB louder (energetic masking), for parts within 20 LU of the mix.

stemDrift.label: Largest stem level change
stemDrift.why: Per-stem loudness relative to the mix vs baseline; catches one part getting much louder or quieter.

gap.label: Longest dropout
gap.why: 400 ms loudness more than 35 LU under the song between the first bar and the final hit (a phantom gap); breakdowns are quieter but not silent. Silence after the final hit is dead air.

leadIn.label: Silence before the music
leadIn.why: Time from play to the first audible note.

contrast.label: Bar loudness spread (p90-p10)
contrast.why: How much bar-by-bar loudness moves across the song; near zero is a flat loop with no arrangement.

peakOverBreak.label: Peak sections over breakdowns
peakOverBreak.why: Loudness of the peak sections (C/G) over the breakdowns (E/F); a drop should land harder than the breakdown before it.

peakOverIntro.label: Peak sections over the intro
peakOverIntro.why: Loudness of the peak sections over the intro (A). Club intros are often full-level for DJs, so only an intro 3 LU louder than the peaks fails.

ringOut.label: Final ring-out (to -40 dB)
ringOut.why: Time for the final hit to decay 40 dB (extrapolated from the decay rate when it outlasts the rendered tail; 999 = not decaying, a stuck note or runaway feedback). A long hall reverb is ~2-5 s.

cutoff.label: Steepest drop in the ending
cutoff.why: Largest 10 ms fall of the ending envelope while still audible; an abrupt truncation shows as a cliff.

deadAir.label: Dead air after the ending
deadAir.why: Time the song keeps running (and the next one waits) after its ring-out has died.

reasons.message: Dead air after the ending 15.8 s (seed 11) > 5
